questions.q: In 'The Stag and His Reflection', what part of himself was the Stag ashamed of?
choices: His thin legs
His antlers
His short tail
His brown coat
questions.evidence: he was very much ashamed of his spindling legs

questions.q: In 'The Stag and His Reflection', why did the Panther catch the Stag?
choices: His antlers got caught in the branches
His thin legs were too slow to run
He stopped to drink at the spring again
He fell asleep in the deep forest
questions.evidence: his wide-spreading antlers caught in the branches of the trees

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Stag and His Reflection'?
choices: We often value pretty things over useful ones
Always drink from a clear and quiet spring
Fast runners will always win in the end
Never go into the forest alone at night
questions.evidence: We often make much of the ornamental and despise the useful.

questions.q: In 'The Peacock', who gave the Peacock his beautiful feathers?
choices: The goddess Juno
The wise old Eagle
Jupiter himself
The Nightingale
questions.evidence: These, Juno, whose favorite he was, granted to him

questions.q: In 'The Peacock', what happened when the Peacock tried to fly after seeing the Eagle?
choices: His heavy train of feathers held him down
He flew even higher than the Eagle could
Juno took all of his feathers away
He crashed into a cloud and fell down
questions.evidence: the weight of his magnificent train held him down

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Peacock'?
choices: Do not give up your freedom just to look fancy
Always ask Juno for whatever you want to have
Eagles are the finest birds that ever flew
Beautiful birds can always fly the highest
questions.evidence: Do not sacrifice your freedom for the sake of pomp and show.

questions.q: In 'The Mice and the Weasels', why could the Mouse leaders not escape into their holes?
choices: Their tall head-dresses would not fit through
They had grown too fat from eating grain
The Weasels stood in front of the holes
They forgot in the fight where the holes were
questions.evidence: the Mouse leaders could not squeeze through the narrow openings because of their head-dresses

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Lean Dog', why did the Dog tell the Wolf to wait a few days before eating him?
choices: He said he would be fat after his master's wedding feast
He said he was very sick and would taste bad to a wolf
He said he had puppies at home that he had to feed first
He said his master would bring the Wolf some meat later
questions.evidence: You can guess how fine and fat I will grow on the scraps from the table

questions.q: In 'The Wolf and the Lean Dog', who was the 'porter' the Dog said would open the door?
choices: A huge Dog that did not like wolves
The master's daughter who opened it
A kind old man who guarded the gate
The Wolf's old friend from the woods
